subject: BrightHealth AI — fee schedule rationalization & SOW edit request
messages:
From: Elena Soto <elena@brighthealth.ai>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Maya Kline <maya.k@brighthealth.ai>
Date: 2027-05-19T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Request: fee schedule amortization + capacity reslice

Hi Marcus,

Hope you're well. We're planning to shift some of our committed GPU capacity from H2 FY27 into H1 to support a new clinical pilot. That will affect the order form: we need to reallocate 450 vGPU-hours/month from Q4 into Q2–Q3, and discuss amortizing the implementation fees across the revised term instead of billing up front.

Can your team produce an addendum (change order) that:
- updates Exhibit A (capacity table) to reflect the redistribution,
- proposes a proration approach for implementation and onboarding fees, and
- includes any pricing adjustments for the shifted ramp (we'd like to avoid a material increase).

I've attached our proposed fee schedule (BrightHealth_Fee_Schedule_Proposed.xlsx) and the current SOW (SOW_BrightHealth_V1.2.docx) for context. Procurement timeline: our legal/procurement needs a redline by EOD Monday 5/24 to present at the review on 5/26.

Could you loop in legal and let us know the expected path/timing? Also confirm who on your side signs the addendum.

Thanks,

Elena Soto
Head of Clinical Partnerships
BrightHealth AI

--
Attachment stubs: BrightHealth_Fee_Schedule_Proposed.xlsx (spreadsheet), SOW_BrightHealth_V1.2.docx (doc)

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwoodinference.com>
To: Elena Soto <elena@brighthealth.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2027-05-19T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: fee schedule amortization + capacity reslice

Elena — thanks for the clear ask and the files. We can do this. Proposed next steps on our side:

1) Internal legal to prepare an MSA addendum + redline to Exhibit A and SOW edits (Laura) — target: draft by 5/21 EOD.
2) Commercial to produce a fee-schedule working version with proration options (me + Karthik) — target: 5/20 midday.
3) Joint review call to walk the redline and pick the proration approach — propose 5/21 10:00 AM PT (30 min).
4) If accepted, we'll route for signatures via DocuSign; we typically have our CRO or GC sign addenda depending on amendment level — will confirm once Laura reviews.

Laura/Karthik — can you confirm availability and whether we should run a short risk/credit check before finalizing the proration (BrightHealth previously requested extended payment terms in Q1)?

Elena — we'll aim to hit your procurement timeline and get the redline back by 5/24 at latest; if we need earlier, let us know and we can accelerate.

Thanks,

Marcus Lin
Sr. Account Lead, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

--
Attachment stubs: none

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwoodinference.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Elena Soto <elena@brighthealth.ai>
Date: 2027-05-21T08:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: fee schedule amortization + capacity reslice

Marcus / Karthik — quick legal note after reviewing the SOW and the proposed fee schedule.

High-level:
- We can accommodate the capacity redistribution via a short-form change order that amends Exhibit A and the SOW. That avoids touching the main MSA clauses.
- For implementation/onboarding fees: recommend amortization across the remaining term with a catch-up clause if BrightHealth reduces total committed capacity before the end of the term. This preserves our economic position while meeting their request.
- Payment terms: if procurement asks for extended net terms, require a credit approval workflow and likely a security deposit or phased billing — flag to commercial.

Redline guidance (attached as MSA_redline_BH_v3.pdf):
- Exhibit A: add a tranche row for 'Q2–Q3 reallocation' with explicit vGPU-hours and effective dates.
- SOW §2 (Implementation fees): edit to add amortization language and tie to termination/true-up mechanics.
- Add a short approval section listing signers (company officer level) to avoid later signature disputes.

Please confirm which proration option commercial will propose (equal monthly amortization vs weighted by expected usage). I can draft language for either. Also tell me whether BrightHealth's procurement wants to treat the onboarding fee as refundable credit if utilization doesn't materialize — that changes the billing approach.

Laura Bennett
Counsel, Commercial Contracts
Redwood Inference

--
Attachment stub: MSA_redline_BH_v3.pdf (annotated redline)

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwoodinference.com>
To: Elena Soto <elena@brighthealth.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2027-05-21T11:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: fee schedule amortization + capacity reslice

Elena — quick update and proposed path.

1) Commercial will circulate two proration options (equal monthly amortization; usage-weighted amortization) by EOD 5/21. Karthik will include a short worked example showing monthly payment impacts.
2) Legal (Laura) has provided a targeted redline that keeps changes to Exhibit A and the SOW; she recommends amortization with a true-up and signatory section. Attached redline PDF will be included in the DocuSign packet.
3) Proposed: 5/24 joint review (30 minutes) to confirm option and finalize redline. If the review lands on 5/24, we can route for signatures the same day; DocuSign link and HubSpot deal update will follow.

Can you confirm:
- whether BrightHealth wants the onboarding fee to be refundable credit or non-refundable but subject to true-up,
- who will sign on BrightHealth's side (title/name) so we can populate the signature block.

If you confirm, we'll lock the addendum for procurement's 5/26 review.

Thanks and talk soon,

Marcus Lin
Sr. Account Lead, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

--
Attachment stubs: SOW_BrightHealth_V1.2.docx (context), BrightHealth_Fee_Schedule_Proposed.xlsx (context), MSA_redline_BH_v3.pdf (legal redline)
